risk: Cargo loss and damage claims are settled without investigating root cause or pursuing recovery from the carrier at fault, so the same losses recur.
audit_objective: Assess whether claims are validated, recovered where a third party is liable, and used to drive corrective action.
what_to_review: Claim intake, validation and settlement authority
Evidence required before settlement — proof of delivery, condition reports, photographs
Recovery from subcontracted carriers and insurers
Root-cause analysis and corrective action on repeat loss points
Claims reserve adequacy and ageing
procedures: Sample settled claims and test that liability was established before payment, not assumed.
Identify claims where a subcontracted carrier held the freight at the time of loss and test whether recovery was pursued within the contractual notice period.
Analyse claims by terminal, lane and commodity to locate concentrations, then test whether any corrective action followed.
Test the ageing of open claims and the basis for the reserve held against them.
Reconcile the claims register to the general ledger loss account and to insurer recoveries.
red_flags: Claims settled below an investigation threshold that is never reviewed in aggregate
Recovery notice periods missed repeatedly
The same terminal appearing in loss concentrations quarter after quarter
Claims paid without proof of delivery on file
evidence: Subcontract carrier agreements and notice terms

risk: Gift card and loyalty balances are manipulated by staff, or breakage is recognised on an assumption that overstates income.
audit_objective: Assess the integrity of stored-value and loyalty balances and the support for breakage recognition.
what_to_review: Gift card activation, reload and void controls at the till
Loyalty point issuance, adjustment and manual accrual rights
Breakage assumption and redemption history supporting it
Reconciliation of the liability to the issuing platform
Employee accounts and their transaction patterns
procedures: Analyse gift card activations reversed or voided shortly after issue, by operator.
Test manual loyalty point adjustments by user and value; sample the largest for approval and business reason.
Match loyalty and gift card accounts to employee records and analyse redemption behaviour on those accounts.
Recompute breakage using the actual redemption curve and compare to the rate recognised.
Reconcile the platform balance to the ledger liability at several dates.
red_flags: Cards activated and voided in the same shift
Points adjusted upward immediately before redemption
Employee-linked accounts with outsized balances
Breakage rate unchanged for years despite behaviour shifts
evidence: Gift card and loyalty platform transaction data

risk: Payments are processed to incorrect or fraudulent beneficiaries, and internal or dormant accounts are used to warehouse the proceeds.
audit_objective: Assess controls over payment execution, beneficiary integrity and the use of internal and dormant accounts.
what_to_review: Payment authorisation limits and dual control by channel
Beneficiary verification and confirmation-of-payee checks
Dormant account reactivation and monitoring
Internal, suspense and staff account usage
Payment recall and error correction process
procedures: Test that every payment channel enforces dual authorisation at the stated thresholds, including manual and urgent routes.
Analyse dormant accounts that reactivated in the period and test the first transaction on each.
Extract transactions on internal and staff accounts and test the business justification for the largest and most frequent.
Sample high-value payments and test beneficiary verification evidence.
Review payment errors and recalls for pattern and for whether root causes were fixed.
red_flags: Urgent payments bypassing dual control
Dormant accounts reactivating just before a large credit
Staff accounts transacting with customer accounts
Beneficiary details changed shortly before payment release
evidence: Payment system transaction logs and authorisation configuration

risk: Aircraft are returned to lessors without meeting contractual return conditions, triggering large end-of-lease compensation claims that were never provided for.
audit_objective: Assess whether lease return obligations are tracked through the lease term and provided for on a supportable basis.
what_to_review: Inventory of lease return conditions per aircraft
Tracking of maintenance status against those conditions
Provisioning for expected return costs
Records and back-to-birth traceability required at return
Negotiation and settlement of end-of-lease claims
procedures: Build a register of return conditions from the lease agreements themselves and compare it to what the business is tracking.
For aircraft returning within two years, compare current maintenance status to the required return condition and quantify the gap.
Test whether the provision reflects that gap or only scheduled maintenance.
Review recent lease returns and compare final settlement to the amount provided.
Test the completeness of component records required at return.
red_flags: Return conditions summarised by the operator rather than read from the lease
Provisions based on maintenance plans, not lease terms
Settlements consistently exceeding provisions
Component records reconstructed close to the return date
evidence: Lease agreements and return condition schedules

risk: Fare rules, refunds and interline settlements are applied incorrectly, so revenue is lost between the booking and the general ledger.
audit_objective: Assess whether flown revenue is complete and correctly valued, and whether refunds and interline balances are controlled.
what_to_review: Fare rule configuration and manual fare overrides
Refund and reissue authority and reason codes
Interline and code-share settlement reconciliation
Agency and distribution channel commission accuracy
Unflown ticket expiry and residual value treatment
procedures: Re-price a sample of tickets from the fare rules and quantify variance to the fare actually charged.
Analyse refunds and reissues by agent and reason code; sample the outliers for authorisation.
Reconcile interline billings to the settlement clearing house statements and test disputes raised within the deadline.
Recompute agency commission for a sample against the distribution agreement.
Test the expiry and recognition of unflown tickets against the stated policy.
red_flags: Manual fare overrides concentrated with a few agents
Refunds issued to a payment method other than the original
Interline disputes filed after the deadline
Expiry recognition accelerated near period end

risk: Food and beverage margin is lost through unrecorded wastage, over-portioning, unauthorised staff meals and supplier short-delivery.
audit_objective: Identify where margin is lost between purchase and sale in food and beverage outlets.
what_to_review: Recipe costing and portion control
Wastage recording and its plausibility
Staff meal and entertainment policy and recording
Goods receipt verification against delivery notes and weights
Void and discount patterns in the outlet point of sale
procedures: Observe service and compare actual portions to the costed recipe for high-volume items.
Compare recorded wastage across outlets and shifts; implausibly low or perfectly consistent wastage warrants challenge.
Test goods receipt for weight and count verification rather than signature only, for a sample of deliveries.
Analyse voids, discounts and staff meals by server and shift against outlet averages.
Reconcile theoretical to actual consumption for a sample of high-value beverage lines.
red_flags: Wastage recorded as the same figure every week
Deliveries signed without verification
Discounts concentrated on particular shifts
Stock counts performed by the outlet manager alone
evidence: Goods receipt records and delivery notes

risk: Fuel uplifted into aircraft is not reconciled to supplier invoices, so the airline pays for volumes it never received.
audit_objective: Confirm that fuel purchased reconciles to fuel uplifted and that pricing follows the supply contract.
what_to_review: Uplift recording at the wing and its independence from the supplier
Reconciliation of uplift tickets to supplier invoices
Contract pricing, differentials and into-plane fees
Density and temperature correction on volumes
Dispute handling with fuel suppliers
procedures: Reconcile uplift volumes from flight records to supplier invoiced volumes by station and quantify the difference.
Re-price a sample of invoices against the contract, including index differentials and into-plane fees.
Test whether volume corrections for temperature and density were applied consistently.
Review the ageing and outcome of fuel supplier disputes.
red_flags: Uplift recorded solely from the supplier ticket
Persistent one-directional variances at a station
Fees charged that are not in the contract
Disputes abandoned rather than resolved

risk: Orders are picked, packed or shipped incorrectly, generating replacement cost, refunds and customer loss that is absorbed as a cost of doing business.
audit_objective: Assess fulfilment accuracy, the cost of getting it wrong, and whether root causes are addressed.
what_to_review: Pick and pack accuracy and verification at despatch
Inventory accuracy between the warehouse and the storefront
Carrier performance and lost parcel handling
Replacement and refund cost attribution
Returns processing and restocking accuracy
procedures: Quantify order defects — wrong item, missing item, damaged — and the total cost of remediation over the period.
Test inventory accuracy by cycle count and compare to the availability shown on the storefront; oversell indicates a control gap.
Analyse lost and damaged parcels by carrier and test whether claims were filed within the carrier deadline.
Trace a sample of returns from receipt to restock or write-off and test the valuation applied.
red_flags: Defect cost recorded in a general expense account with no attribution
Overselling followed by silent cancellation
Carrier claims not filed
Returned stock restocked without inspection

risk: Third-party sellers list counterfeit, unsafe or prohibited products, exposing the platform to regulatory action and liability.
audit_objective: Assess whether sellers and their listings are vetted and monitored proportionately to the risk they carry.
what_to_review: Seller identity verification and business registration checks
Prohibited and restricted product controls at listing
Counterfeit and intellectual property complaint handling
Product safety recalls and takedown speed
Seller performance monitoring and suspension
procedures: Sample sellers and test that identity and business verification was completed before listing was enabled.
Test the listing filters by attempting to list restricted categories in a test environment.
Trace a sample of intellectual property and safety complaints through to takedown and measure elapsed time.
Test whether sellers suspended for cause reappear under new identities by matching bank details, addresses and devices.
red_flags: Sellers onboarded with unverified documents
Restricted items reachable through alternate category paths
Takedowns taking weeks
Suspended sellers returning with the same bank account

risk: Regulatory obligations under the licence or determination are not tracked to an owner, so breaches are discovered by the regulator rather than internally.
audit_objective: Confirm that licence and determination obligations are identified, owned, monitored and evidenced.
what_to_review: Completeness of the regulatory obligation register against the licence
Ownership and monitoring of each obligation
Accuracy of performance data submitted to the regulator
Self-reporting of breaches and their timeliness
Regulatory penalties, undertakings and remediation
procedures: Read the licence and determination and build an obligation list independently; compare it to the register in use and quantify the gaps.
Sample obligations and test for evidence of compliance in the period, not merely an assertion of compliance.
Re-perform the calculation of key performance measures submitted to the regulator from source data.
Test breach self-reporting against the required timeframe and review whether remediation commitments were delivered.
red_flags: Obligations without a named owner
Performance figures that cannot be reconstructed from source
Breaches identified by the regulator first
Remediation commitments closed without evidence
evidence: Submitted regulatory returns and source data

risk: The reinsurance programme does not respond as expected to a large loss because cover, exclusions or aggregate limits were not understood when the risk was written.
audit_objective: Assess whether the reinsurance programme actually covers the exposures being underwritten.
what_to_review: Alignment between underwriting appetite and reinsurance cover
Exclusions, aggregate limits and reinstatement provisions
Placement completeness and signed slips before inception
Reinsurer security and credit concentration
Recovery process after a large loss
procedures: Map material underwriting exposures against the reinsurance programme and identify uncovered aggregations.
Test that binding slips were signed and complete before cover incepted, not retrospectively.
Model a large-loss scenario and trace the expected recovery through the programme including reinstatements.
Assess reinsurer concentration and credit ratings against policy limits.
Review actual recoveries from recent large losses against what was expected.
red_flags: Cover placed after inception
Aggregate limits exhausted without anyone noticing
Reliance on a small number of reinsurers
Recoveries materially below expectation after a loss

risk: Reserves are influenced by earnings pressure rather than actuarial judgement, and adverse development is not surfaced to the board on a timely basis.
audit_objective: Assess the independence and rigour of the reserving process and the transparency of reserve movements.
what_to_review: Independence of the actuarial function from underwriting and claims
Reserving methodology, assumption setting and change control
Management adjustments to the actuarial central estimate
Reserve development triangles and back-testing
Reporting of adverse development to the board
procedures: Analyse historical reserve development and quantify how often and in which direction estimates have proved wrong.
Test the size, direction and justification of management adjustments to the actuarial estimate across several periods.
Test whether assumption changes were documented and approved before results were known.
Review board and committee papers for whether adverse development was reported plainly or netted against other movements.
red_flags: Management adjustments always favourable
Assumption changes made after preliminary results circulate
Consistent adverse development in the same class of business
Reserving committee minutes recording no challenge
evidence: Actuarial reserve reports and development triangles

risk: Rooms are sold through channels at rates and commissions that destroy margin, and rate parity or contractual terms with distributors are breached.
audit_objective: Assess whether distribution channel economics are understood, controlled and compliant with distributor agreements.
what_to_review: Channel mix and net rate after commission by channel
Rate parity obligations and breaches
Commission calculation accuracy and reconciliation
Overbooking, walk cost and compensation
Group and corporate contract rate adherence
procedures: Recompute net revenue per room night by channel after commission and compare to the direct channel.
Test rate parity by comparing published rates across channels on sample dates.
Reconcile commission invoiced by distributors to the bookings actually delivered and recompute against the agreement.
Quantify walk and compensation costs from overbooking and test the authorisation for compensation paid.
red_flags: Channels with negative contribution still receiving allocation
Parity breaches unnoticed until a distributor claims
Commission paid on cancelled bookings
Compensation paid without approval
evidence: Property management and channel manager data

risk: Trade investment is committed without evidence that it generates incremental volume, and accruals are settled against claims that were never validated.
audit_objective: Assess whether trade spend is authorised, delivered, validated and generating a return.
what_to_review: Promotion approval, expected uplift and post-event evaluation
Deduction and claim validation before settlement
Accrual accuracy and the ageing of unsettled claims
Customer-level profitability including all trade investment
Authority limits on discretionary spend
procedures: Select major promotions and compare actual uplift to the volume assumed in the approval; test whether any post-event evaluation occurred.
Sample settled customer deductions and test for a matched, approved promotion and delivery evidence.
Analyse the ageing of open deductions and the rate at which disputes are simply written off.
Recompute customer profitability including all trade investment and identify customers who are loss-making after spend.
red_flags: Post-event evaluation performed for none of the largest promotions
Deductions written off once they age past a threshold
Spend approved by the same person who negotiates the customer relationship
Promotions repeated annually with no measured return

risk: Traders conceal losses or breach limits through mispriced trades, off-market transactions or unauthorised products.
audit_objective: Assess the independence and effectiveness of controls over trading activity and valuation.
what_to_review: Independence of risk control and back office from the trading desk
Limit framework, monitoring and breach escalation
Independent price verification and off-market trade detection
Trader mandates, approved products and counterparties
Mandatory leave and trade cancellation or amendment patterns
procedures: Test independent price verification by re-valuing a sample of positions from an external curve.
Analyse trade amendments and cancellations by trader, and trades executed at prices away from the market at execution time.
Test limit breaches for timely escalation and for whether limits were subsequently raised rather than positions reduced.
Confirm mandatory leave was actually taken by all trading staff and that their books were managed by others during it.
Test that all traded products and counterparties are on the approved list.
red_flags: Amendments concentrated with one trader
Limits raised shortly after a breach
Positions valued using trader-supplied marks
Mandatory leave waived for key staff
evidence: Trade capture system extracts with amendment history

risk: Liquidity and capital positions are managed on assumptions that do not hold under stress, leaving the bank exposed to a funding shock or a regulatory shortfall.
audit_objective: Assess whether liquidity and capital are measured, stressed and governed on a defensible basis.
what_to_review: Liquidity risk appetite, limits and early warning indicators
Stress testing scenarios, severity and governance
Funding concentration and deposit stickiness assumptions
Capital planning and buffer management
Contingency funding plan credibility and testing
procedures: Test the data feeding liquidity metrics back to source systems for completeness and accuracy.
Challenge stress scenario severity against historical and regulatory benchmarks, and test whether results drive any action.
Analyse deposit behaviour against the stickiness assumptions used in the liquidity model.
Review the contingency funding plan and test whether it has ever been exercised.
Test capital projections against the plan and the sensitivity of the buffer to the stress scenarios.
red_flags: Stress scenarios milder than events already experienced
Early warning indicators breached without action
Model assumptions unchanged through a rate cycle
Contingency funding plan never tested
evidence: Liquidity and capital reporting and source data
kpis: Date of last funding plan test

risk: Risks are written outside appetite or priced below technical rates to hold volume, so the portfolio deteriorates before the loss ratio reveals it.
audit_objective: Assess whether underwriting stays within appetite and authority, and whether pricing is technically supported.
what_to_review: Underwriting authority by class, limit and referral triggers
Adherence to the technical rate and the level of discounting
Risk selection against stated appetite and exclusions
Peer review of large or unusual risks
Delegated underwriting authority given to third parties
procedures: Sample bound risks and test each against the underwriter's authority and the referral criteria.
Quantify the discount to technical rate by underwriter, class and broker, and test the justification for the deepest discounts.
Test that risks outside appetite were declined or properly referred and approved.
Review peer review coverage and whether reviewers ever changed an outcome.
For delegated authorities, test the binder terms, reporting received and any audits performed on the coverholder.
red_flags: Discounting deepest at period end
Referral triggers narrowly avoided through structuring
Peer review recorded but never dissenting
Coverholders writing outside the binder with no audit
evidence: Policy bordereaux and bound risk data
